anti_patterns: Unbounded minter role: wrapped token with public or single-EOA mint function allowing unauthorized issuance
Minting on unfinalized lock proofs: acting on latest-block events without finality wait or reorg handling
Single-relayer attestation: one off-chain signer authorizing mints with no quorum or fallback verifier
Reusing one vault for unrelated tokens without accounting isolation: one exploit unbacks every wrapped asset
Missing nonce/idempotency on mint: same lock proof redeemable twice on the destination chain
Treating wrapped tokens as canonical: routing unrelated liquidity against bridge-specific IOUs as if fungible
avoid_when: You control the token contract and can grant mint/burn roles: prefer burn-and-mint for unified supply and no idle collateral
Sub-second finality is required: two-chain lock, attestation, and mint latency cannot meet low-latency budgets
No trustworthy attestation network exists for the chain pair: without finalized-proof verification there is no safe mint trigger
Locked collateral cannot remain solvent custodied indefinitely: idle TVL opportunity cost or regulatory custody constraints dominate
Only same-chain wrapping is needed: single-chain WETH-style deposit/mint has no cross-chain proof problem
benefits: Bridges assets the bridge does not control: native ETH, BTC, or existing ERC-20s with no mint/burn hooks can move cross-chain
Verifiable 1:1 backing invariant: locked_tokens_on_source equals outstanding wrapped supply, auditable via proof-of-reserve
Hub-and-spoke reuse: one LockRelease pool on the native chain pairs with BurnMint pools on many destination chains
No token contract changes: standard ERC-20 transferFrom/transfer suffices on the lock side (CCIP LockRelease pools need no burner/minter roles)
Redeemability: any holder of the wrapped token can burn it and reclaim the original via the symmetric burn-and-unlock leg
Per-lane controls: rate limits, remote-pool allowlists, and fees attach at the pool as the issuer control point
best_practices: Wait for source-chain finality before attesting: never mint on unfinalized lock events; document the reorg window per chain
Key mint/burn behind a quorum or decentralized verifier (multisig, oracle network, light client), never a single EOA
Enforce per-message idempotency with unique nonces: reject already-processed lock/burn proofs to block replay double-mint
Maintain remote-pool allowlists in both directions so each pool only accepts proofs from its configured counterpart
Configure per-lane rate limits and circuit breakers to bound exploit blast radius (CCIP token pools ship native rate limiting)
Track locked-versus-outstanding accounting on-chain and expose proof-of-reserve for auditors
Provide a refund/claim path for partial completion: locked-but-never-minted deposits must be recoverable
Pause-and-migrate procedure for pool upgrades: move vault liquidity (e.g. into the new lockbox) before cutting the registry over
component_types: Vault / Lockbox: source-chain escrow custodying originals and emitting nonce-keyed Deposit events
Wrapped Token: destination-chain ERC-20 with onlyBridge mint/burn (e.g. IBurnMintERC20 mint and burn)
Attestation Network: validator set, oracle network, or light client verifying lock finality and authorizing mints
Minter Controller: destination minter contract validating proofs, nonces, and destination chain/account before minting
Burn Handler: destination burn entrypoint signaling the reverse leg for unlock on the source chain
Pool Registry: per-chain token-to-pool mapping and remote-pool configuration (TokenAdminRegistry pattern)
Relayer / Messaging Layer: transports verified lock/burn proofs between chains (e.g. CCIP OnRamp/OffRamp)
Rate Limiter and Circuit Breaker: per-lane transfer caps and emergency pause on the pools
context: Moving asset value from a source chain to a destination chain that share no state, for a token the bridge does not control. Originals are locked in a custodial vault on the source chain making them provably unspendable; an attestation network observes the finalized lock event and a privileged minter issues a 1:1 wrapped representation on the destination. Redemption reverses the flow: burn wrapped tokens on the destination, attest the burn, unlock originals on the source
design_principles: Backing Invariant First: locked_tokens_on_source must always equal outstanding wrapped supply; every design decision defends this equality
Never Mint on Unfinalized Proof: mint authority fires only on finalized, quorum-verified lock evidence
Least-Privilege Minting: only the verified bridge adapter can call mint/burn; no public mint path exists
Idempotent Redemption: each lock/burn proof executes at most once via nonces and processed-proof registries
Assume No Atomicity: lock and mint are separate transactions; design explicit paths for partial completion and chain reorgs
Bound the Honeypot: isolate vault accounting per token and cap per-lane exposure with rate limits
Symmetric Return Leg: burn-and-unlock mirrors lock-and-mint with the same proof rigor, never a shortcut
name: lock-mint-bridge
technology_stack: Solidity (ERC-20 vault, wrapped token with onlyBridge mint/burn)
Light clients / block-header relays with Merkle inclusion proofs
tradeoffs: Custody honeypot: the vault concentrates all locked TVL; if drained, every wrapped token becomes unbacked (Wormhole February 2022: 120,000 wETH minted without backing)
Idle capital: locked collateral sits unproductive indefinitely, with opportunity cost scaling alongside bridged TVL
No atomicity: lock and mint are separate transactions, so reorgs and relayer outages create locked-but-never-minted states needing refund paths
Wrapped fragmentation: each bridge issues its own IOU (Wormhole ETH differs from LayerZero ETH), splitting liquidity and multiplying depeg surfaces
Two-chain latency and fees: lock gas plus attestation plus mint gas, paced by the slower chain's finality
Attestation trust dependence: minter-key or validator-set compromise enables unbounded unbacked minting
use_cases: Bridging native ETH to a rollup or sidechain as a wrapped ERC-20 (canonical L2 bridges)
Wrapping BTC/ETH for use in destination-chain DeFi while originals stay custodied on the source chain
Hub-and-spoke issuance: one native-chain LockRelease pool paired with wrapped minters on several destination chains
Permissionless wrapping of third-party ERC-20s the bridge issuer does not control
Redemption flows where holders burn wrapped tokens to reclaim originals on the native chain
